speaker: Kimi K3
text: Infy's 5-year CAGR of -5.1% and a 39% drop from its all-time high tell you the business has been shrinking in dollar terms while the stock keeps paying a 4% yield — that's a value trap, not a compounder. On the IPO question: with $10 you can't even meet the typical $150–$200 minimum lot on a US zero-commission broker, so the only realistic path is a SPAC or direct listing that allows fractional allocation, which are rare. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery, the round-trip bill on ₹10,000 is ₹38.15 (STT ₹20, exchange ₹0.59, SEBI ₹0.02, stamp ₹1.5, GST ₹0.11, DP ₹15.93) — 0.38% breakeven before the 20% short-term gains tax if you sell within a year. Auto and battery names like Tata Motors, Mahindra, Exide or Amara Raja all trade above ₹10,000 per share, so your ₹10k budget buys zero whole shares; you'd need a fractional-enabled platform or a smaller-cap EV-ancillary stock.

speaker: Kimi K3
text: HDFC Bank's 30% drop from its peak and 11x forward P/E look optically cheap, but the 28.9% YTD slide in 2026 while Nifty only fell ~1.7% signals real fundamental pressure — likely margin compression from the 4.99% US 10-year yield and Brent at $116.72 squeezing net interest margins. The 3.8% dividend yield is the only cushion, yet with 21.3% earnings growth priced in, any miss on the January 16 earnings could trigger another leg down given the 1.08 beta. On your auto/battery wish list: Amara Raja (~₹1,200) and Exide (~₹400) fit the ₹10k whole-share budget, but both trade at 25-30x earnings with flat volume growth — not the 10x compounders you need. For the US side, $100 fractional in NVDA at 63.6% decade CAGR gets you to ~$12.50 in a year, not $1,000; the math simply doesn't work without leverage or lottery tickets.
